management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Appendicitis — IV access — 16G or larger; Analgesia: morphine 2.5–5 mg IV (DO NOT withhold — does not mask diagnosis); Anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg IV; IV fluid: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's 1 L over 2–4 h; Nil by mouth; Bladder: ensure patient has voided (exclude pregnancy in women of childbearing age); Pregnancy test (urine β-hCG) in all females 12–55 years

Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Pancreatitis — IV access + moderate goal-directed IV fluids: Hartmann's 10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h, reassessed at 12–24 h — avoid aggressive fluids (WATERFALL 2022; ACG 2024); Analgesia: morphine IV (superior to pethidine — ignore old advice); Anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg IV; Nil by mouth initially (clear fluids once pain improves — within 24–48 h in mild cases); Oxygen if SpO₂ <95% or respiratory compromise; IDC if haemodynamically unstable (target urine output >0.5 mL/kg/h)

expectations.note: USPSTF 2021 / ACG 2021: average-risk screening from 45. ACG 2021: one FDR with CRC diagnosed < 60 (father at 58) → colonoscopy from age 40 (or 10 years before the relative’s age at diagnosis), repeated every 5 years — so he is overdue on the ACG reading. BSG 2020 (UK) would not add colonoscopic surveillance for a single FDR diagnosed ≥ 50. The practice’s policy needs the surgeon’s decision. Not observable in the web harness: the dashboard feeds the Family History field (ClinicalPromptsStrip familyHistory) to computeClinicalPrompts, but the vignette schema has no family-history input, so web-runner passes []. In the dashboard the "FHx colorectal cancer, age 35–49" prompt would probably add a colonoscopy. Needs a familyHistory input in the schema and both runners. Without a family history there is no screening prompt before 50: the average-risk "colorectal_screen" prompt starts at age 50 (USPSTF 2021 and ACG 2021: 45) and offers FOBT every 2 years rather than annual FIT. management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Cholecystitis — IV access + IV fluids (Hartmann's 1 L over 4 h); ⚠ RENAL: withheld (contains diclofenac) — NSAIDs contraindicated in AKI, severe CKD or a solitary obstructed kidney (NICE NG148 2019; BNF). Use paracetamol ± an opioid.; Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; Nil by mouth if surgical management planned; Temperature, HR, BP monitoring
Schedule: repeat obs in 2 h — Monitor Acute Cholecystitis — current state: Tokyo Grade II (Moderate). Recheck vitals and labs in 2 hours.
Schedule: Acute Cholecystitis — Required within 4 hours — HDU / Step-down.
Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
IV access + IV fluids (0.9% NaCl 1 L over 4–6h)
Analgesia: morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM + antiemetic
Antibiotics: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2 g IV 8-hourly (or piperacillin-tazobactam if severe)
NBM / low-fat diet
Consider early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72h (Grade I–II Tokyo)
Surgical referral / admission
Repeat USS if not improving at 24–48h
Peri-operative (patient-specific):
Fasting: food up to 6 h and clear fluids up to 2 h before anaesthesia (AAGBI 2010; ESA 2011).
Antibiotic prophylaxis: single dose at induction per the local antimicrobial policy (SIGN 104 high-risk laparoscopic cholecystectomy); check the allergy record.
Paracetamol 1g QDS (regular); NSAIDs avoided (renal impairment, age ≥ 75, heart failure — NICE NG148; BNF).
Post-operative antibiotics are not needed after cholecystectomy for TG18 Grade I–II acute cholecystitis; continue only for complicated disease (gangrene, perforation, abscess) (TG18).
PATIENT-SPECIFIC SAFETY CHECKS (review before acting):

[WARNING] VTE prophylaxis (NICE NG89): assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission and after surgery (NG89, 2018). Mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) unless contraindicated (e.g. peripheral arterial disease), plus LMWH dose-adjusted for renal function — eGFR/CrCl 28 mL/min: enoxaparin 20 mg SC once daily or unfractionated heparin (BNF) — from 6–12 h after surgery if bleeding risk allows, for at least 7 days.

[WARNING] Frailty / delirium risk (frail, age 88): delirium prevention and 4AT screening (NICE CG103); comprehensive geriatric assessment and elderly-medicine (geriatric) input; shared decision-making with goals of care and a treatment-escalation plan documented (CPOC 2021 perioperative care for people living with frailty).
[INFO] Beta-blocker (bisoprolol): tachycardia may be blunted — heart rate can under-read shock or sepsis (ATLS 10).
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Early cholecystectomy (within 72 h or index admission) — Tokyo Guidelines — Grade I/II: early lap cholecystectomy preferred
Interventional Radiology (Urgent (2 wk)): Percutaneous cholecystostomy if high surgical risk
Post-cholecystectomy review 2 weeks.
Investigations: FBC, LFTs, Amylase / Lipase, CT Abdomen/Pelvis.
Surgical pearls: Never divide a structure until Critical View of Safety is confirmed; Early lap cholecystectomy (within 72 h) is superior to delayed — shorter stay, same safety.
Review: 4–6 weeks; return if: Jaundice post-op (CBD stone or injury), Fever, RUQ pain (bile collection, abscess).

management.text: EMERGENCY — Act Now: Sepsis — Initiate 1-Hour Bundle — Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics; IV antibiotics within 1 hour if suspected infection (broad-spectrum; narrow when cultures return); IV crystalloid 30 mL/kg over 3 h if lactate ≥4 or hypotension; Vasopressors (noradrenaline) if MAP <65 despite resuscitation; Measure serum lactate; repeat if initial ≥2 mmol/L; Identify and control source (imaging ± surgical intervention)

O₂ (target SpO₂ >94%)
IV access × 2 + blood cultures before antibiotics
IV broad-spectrum antibiotics: tazobactam/piperacillin 4.5g 8-hourly + metronidazole 500mg TDS
IV fluid resuscitation: 500 mL crystalloid bolus → reassess
Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance
Serial lactate
NBM + NG tube on free drainage
Analgesia: IV morphine (do not withhold)
Urgent surgical review
OPERATIVE MANAGEMENT (most require surgery):
PERFORATED PU:
Laparoscopic washout + omental patch (Graham's patch)
Open repair if laparoscopy contraindicated / contamination heavy
COLONIC PERFORATION:

POST-OPERATIVE: proton pump inhibitor IV → oral; H. pylori eradication (PU)

Selected cases: IV antibiotics + strict monitoring + CT at 48h

management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Small Bowel Obstruction — Lactate 2.4 mmol/L: Tissue hypoperfusion — goal-directed IV fluid resuscitation, reassess in 2 h; IV access + Hartmann's 1–2 L over 2–4 h (bowel obstruction causes significant third-space loss); Analgesia: morphine IV (reassess regularly); Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; NG tube (nasogastric decompression): wide-bore, free drainage + aspirate every hour; IDC for urine output monitoring; Nil by mouth
Schedule: Small Bowel Obstruction — Required within 4 hours — HDU / Step-down.
Repeat lactate in 2 h — Lactate ≥2 — clearance target ≥10% per hour in sepsis resuscitation.
Schedule: repeat obs in 2 h — Monitor Small Bowel Obstruction — current state: Complete SBO. Recheck vitals and labs in 2 hours.
IMMEDIATE:
NBM; IV access × 2; urinary catheter (fluid balance)
IV crystalloid resuscitation: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's
Nasogastric tube (NG) on free drainage — decompress + reduce vomiting
IV antiemetic: ondansetron 8 mg or metoclopramide 10 mg
Analgesia: IV morphine 2.5–5 mg titrated (do not withhold — does not mask signs)
Electrolyte replacement (K⁺ particularly)
CONSERVATIVE TRIAL (adhesion SBO, no signs of strangulation):
48–72h NG decompression + IV fluids; serial clinical examination
Water-soluble contrast study (Gastrografin) at 24 h — therapeutic + diagnostic; adhesive SBO without strangulation only — not for a hernia, closed-loop or strangulated obstruction (WSES/Bologna 2017)
80% adhesion SBO resolves conservatively
OPERATIVE INDICATIONS:
Strangulation (peritonism, fever, leucocytosis, lactate rise, blood supply)
Complete obstruction failing conservative × 48–72h
Hernia (external) causing obstruction → emergency surgery (hernia repair ± bowel resection); do not attempt reduction if strangulation is suspected (WSES 2017)
Tumour / volvulus / intussusception → surgery
Surgical options: adhesiolysis, hernia repair, resection ± anastomosis
Broad-spectrum antibiotics if operative: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV or cefuroxime + metronidazole

IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)

POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis; obstructed infected or solitary kidney → emergency decompression (EAU 2024); bladder outflow obstruction → urethral catheter, monitor for post-obstructive diuresis (hourly urine output, replace losses); avoid NSAIDs in AKI
Stop / withhold NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics and metformin during AKI; restart when renal function recovers (NICE NG148); urinalysis (dipstick) for every patient with AKI
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia (e.g. diarrhoea, high-output stoma): volume replacement — 500 mL 0.9% sodium chloride (or balanced crystalloid) bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): assess volume status; diuretics only for fluid overload, not to treat AKI (NICE NG148)
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ ≥6.5 or ECG changes: calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV over 5–10 min (or calcium chloride 10% 10 mL) — cardioprotection (UK Kidney Association 2023)
⚠ K⁺ 3.3 mmol/L: potassium-shifting treatment withheld — it is for K⁺ ≥ 6.0 mmol/L (UKKA 2023); treat the cause and repeat K⁺.
⚠ K⁺ 3.3 mmol/L: nebulised salbutamol withheld — an adjunct for severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ ≥ 6.5 mmol/L) only (UKKA 2023).
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs

management.text: EMERGENCY — Act Now: Incarcerated / Strangulated Hernia — IV access + prompt fluid resuscitation (up to 30 mL/kg if haemodynamically unstable — SSC 2021); IV analgesia + anti-emetic; NG tube if obstructed (bilious vomiting, distension); Nil by mouth; Attempted manual reduction (taxis) ONLY if: <6 h duration, no peritonism, no systemic compromise — gentle sustained pressure with sedation/analgesia; Do NOT attempt taxis if peritonism, systemic sepsis or suspected ischaemia; Urgent surgical consent for emergency hernia repair

Urgent (< 4 h): Small Bowel Obstruction — IV access + Hartmann's 1–2 L over 2–4 h (bowel obstruction causes significant third-space loss); Analgesia: morphine IV (reassess regularly); Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; NG tube (nasogastric decompression): wide-bore, free drainage + aspirate every hour; IDC for urine output monitoring; Nil by mouth

Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Appendicitis — IV access — 16G or larger; Analgesia: morphine 2.5–5 mg IV (DO NOT withhold — does not mask diagnosis); Anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg IV; IV fluid: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's 1 L over 2–4 h; Nil by mouth; Bladder: ensure patient has voided (exclude pregnancy in women of childbearing age); Pregnancy test (urine β-hCG) in all females 12–55 years

Semi-urgent (< 24 h): Acute Diverticulitis — Analgesia: paracetamol 1 g IV or morphine if severe; IV access if unable to tolerate oral; Fluid resuscitation if dehydrated; Nil by mouth initially if vomiting or surgery anticipated

management.text: EMERGENCY — Act Now: Sepsis — Initiate 1-Hour Bundle — Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics; IV antibiotics within 1 hour if suspected infection (broad-spectrum; narrow when cultures return); IV crystalloid 30 mL/kg over 3 h if lactate ≥4 or hypotension; Vasopressors (noradrenaline) if MAP <65 despite resuscitation; Measure serum lactate; repeat if initial ≥2 mmol/L; Identify and control source (imaging ± surgical intervention)

Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Pancreatitis — Lactate 3.4 mmol/L: Tissue hypoperfusion — goal-directed IV fluid resuscitation, reassess in 2 h; IV access + moderate goal-directed IV fluids: Hartmann's 10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h, reassessed at 12–24 h — avoid aggressive fluids (WATERFALL 2022; ACG 2024); Analgesia: morphine IV (superior to pethidine — ignore old advice); Anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg IV; Nil by mouth initially (clear fluids once pain improves — within 24–48 h in mild cases); Oxygen if SpO₂ <95% or respiratory compromise; IDC if haemodynamically unstable (target urine output >0.5 mL/kg/h)
Schedule: Acute Pancreatitis — Required within 4 hours — Resuscitation Bay / ITU.
Repeat lactate in 2 h — Lactate ≥2 — clearance target ≥10% per hour in sepsis resuscitation.
ADMIT — monitor fluid balance strictly

IV fluids: MODERATE goal-directed resuscitation with Hartmann's — 10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h, reassessed at 12–24 h; avoid aggressive rates, lower in heart failure / renal impairment (WATERFALL 2022; ACG 2024)
No prophylactic antibiotics — antibiotics only for documented infection (ACG 2024; IAP/APA)
Analgesia: morphine IV/IM + antiemetic
NBM initially; early oral/NG feeding within 24–48h if tolerated (reduces complications)
Glasgow / Ranson scoring at 48h

PATIENT-SPECIFIC SAFETY CHECKS (review before acting):

[WARNING] Long-term glucocorticoid (prednisolone): do not stop it. If ≥ 5 mg prednisolone (or equivalent) for > 4 weeks, give steroid cover — hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction or at the start of the acute illness, then 200 mg/24 h (infusion, or 50 mg IV/IM 6-hourly) while unwell or nil by mouth, then double the usual oral dose for 48 h (AAGBI/Society for Endocrinology 2020).

[WARNING] VTE prophylaxis (NICE NG89): assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission and after surgery (NG89, 2018). Mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) unless contraindicated (e.g. peripheral arterial disease), plus LMWH — e.g. enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily, dose-adjust in renal impairment — CrCl < 30 mL/min: 20 mg once daily (BNF) — from 6–12 h after surgery if bleeding risk allows, for at least 7 days.

[WARNING] Frailty / delirium risk (delirium, age 79): delirium prevention and 4AT screening (NICE CG103); comprehensive geriatric assessment and elderly-medicine (geriatric) input; shared decision-making with goals of care and a treatment-escalation plan documented (CPOC 2021 perioperative care for people living with frailty).

SUPERFICIAL SSI (skin / subcutaneous):
Open wound (remove sutures / staples over infected area)

DEEP SSI (below fascia / organ/space):
CT abdomen/pelvis to identify collection
Radiological drainage (USS/CT-guided) where accessible

IV antibiotics: tazobactam/piperacillin 4.5 g 8-hourly (broad spectrum)
WOUND DEHISCENCE (burst abdomen):
Wet pack wound immediately; do NOT attempt primary closure in ward

CT first — assess extent; fistula
May require mesh removal (especially if chronic / biofilm)
Prolonged antibiotic course: culture-guided × 6+ weeks

Extreme pain out of proportion, crepitus, rapidly advancing → EMERGENCY OT

management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Small Bowel Obstruction — IV access + Hartmann's 1–2 L over 2–4 h (bowel obstruction causes significant third-space loss); Analgesia: morphine IV (reassess regularly); Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; NG tube (nasogastric decompression): wide-bore, free drainage + aspirate every hour; IDC for urine output monitoring; Nil by mouth
Schedule: Small Bowel Obstruction — Required within 4 hours — HDU / Step-down.
Schedule: repeat obs in 2 h — Monitor Small Bowel Obstruction — current state: Complete SBO. Recheck vitals and labs in 2 hours.
Trend CRP vs. prior — Compare current CRP with previous result to assess treatment response / progression.
IMMEDIATE:
NBM; IV access × 2; urinary catheter (fluid balance)
IV crystalloid resuscitation: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's
Nasogastric tube (NG) on free drainage — decompress + reduce vomiting
IV antiemetic: ondansetron 8 mg or metoclopramide 10 mg
Analgesia: IV morphine 2.5–5 mg titrated (do not withhold — does not mask signs)
Electrolyte replacement (K⁺ particularly)
CONSERVATIVE TRIAL (adhesion SBO, no signs of strangulation):
48–72h NG decompression + IV fluids; serial clinical examination
Water-soluble contrast study (Gastrografin) at 24 h — therapeutic + diagnostic; adhesive SBO without strangulation only — not for a hernia, closed-loop or strangulated obstruction (WSES/Bologna 2017)
80% adhesion SBO resolves conservatively
OPERATIVE INDICATIONS:
Strangulation (peritonism, fever, leucocytosis, lactate rise, blood supply)
Complete obstruction failing conservative × 48–72h
Hernia (external) causing obstruction → emergency surgery (hernia repair ± bowel resection); do not attempt reduction if strangulation is suspected (WSES 2017)
Tumour / volvulus / intussusception → surgery
Surgical options: adhesiolysis, hernia repair, resection ± anastomosis
Broad-spectrum antibiotics if operative: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV or cefuroxime + metronidazole
PATIENT-SPECIFIC SAFETY CHECKS (review before acting):

[WARNING] VTE prophylaxis (NICE NG89): assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission and after surgery (NG89, 2018). Mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) unless contraindicated (e.g. peripheral arterial disease), plus LMWH — e.g. enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily, dose-adjust in renal impairment — CrCl < 30 mL/min: 20 mg once daily (BNF) — from 6–12 h after surgery if bleeding risk allows, for at least 7 days.
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Laparotomy / adhesiolysis if conservative management fails (>48 h) — CT abdomen/pelvis to confirm and assess for strangulation
Emergency Department (Emergency): Admit for fluid resuscitation + NG decompression
Follow-up at 2–6 weeks post-operatively. Bowel function review. Recurrence counselling.
Review within 24–48 hours.

Trend CRP vs. prior — Compare current CRP with previous result to assess treatment response / progression.

Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Small Bowel Obstruction (P=98%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
IMMEDIATE:
NBM; IV access × 2; urinary catheter (fluid balance)
IV crystalloid resuscitation: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's
Nasogastric tube (NG) on free drainage — decompress + reduce vomiting
IV antiemetic: ondansetron 8 mg or metoclopramide 10 mg
Analgesia: IV morphine 2.5–5 mg titrated (do not withhold — does not mask signs)
Electrolyte replacement (K⁺ particularly)
CONSERVATIVE TRIAL (adhesion SBO, no signs of strangulation):
48–72h NG decompression + IV fluids; serial clinical examination
Water-soluble contrast study (Gastrografin) at 24 h — therapeutic + diagnostic; adhesive SBO without strangulation only — not for a hernia, closed-loop or strangulated obstruction (WSES/Bologna 2017)
80% adhesion SBO resolves conservatively
OPERATIVE INDICATIONS:
Strangulation (peritonism, fever, leucocytosis, lactate rise, blood supply)
Complete obstruction failing conservative × 48–72h
Hernia (external) causing obstruction → emergency surgery (hernia repair ± bowel resection); do not attempt reduction if strangulation is suspected (WSES 2017)
Tumour / volvulus / intussusception → surgery
Surgical options: adhesiolysis, hernia repair, resection ± anastomosis
Broad-spectrum antibiotics if operative: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV or cefuroxime + metronidazole
PATIENT-SPECIFIC SAFETY CHECKS (review before acting):

[WARNING] Insulin-treated diabetes: continue basal (long-acting) insulin — never omit it; give 80% of the usual dose the evening before and on the day; variable-rate IV insulin if more than one meal will be missed; capillary glucose and ketone monitoring; first on the list where possible (CPOC 2021).

[WARNING] VTE prophylaxis (NICE NG89): assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission and after surgery (NG89, 2018). Mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) unless contraindicated (e.g. peripheral arterial disease), plus LMWH — e.g. enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily, dose-adjust in renal impairment — CrCl < 30 mL/min: 20 mg once daily (BNF) — from 6–12 h after surgery if bleeding risk allows, for at least 7 days.
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Laparotomy / adhesiolysis if conservative management fails (>48 h) — CT abdomen/pelvis to confirm and assess for strangulation
Emergency Department (Emergency): Admit for fluid resuscitation + NG decompression
Follow-up at 2–6 weeks post-operatively. Bowel function review. Recurrence counselling.
Review within 24–48 hours.
